title: Scientific result catalogue
scope: Reproduction map for the four main figures, substantive mathematical results, Appendices S1–S7, the mathematics guide, worked estimation example and additional teaching tools.

conventions.python: Python commands assume the numeric environment described in REPRODUCING.md is active. Shell launchers prepare it when needed.
conventions.commands: Command IDs below expand to exact invocations; result records refer to them.
conventions.inputs: Generated parameters and seeds are in the cited code unless an input file is listed. Reference files are comparison records, not necessarily estimator inputs.
conventions.undefined: JSON null denotes an undefined quantity, not zero.
conventions.proofs: Theoretical claims require their stated assumptions and analytical derivations. Finite numerical checks are examples and implementation checks, not general proofs.
conventions.output_locations: Default scientific analyses write outputs/. Visual rebuilds update the explicitly listed tutorial artifacts.
conventions.simulation: Archive summarisation and a fresh SLiM run are different commands.

main_figures.description: Generate the four main figures from recorded parameters and seeds.

core_mathematics.description: Check 30 matrix cases, coordinate changes, proportional scaling, bounds and scalar trajectories.

result_checks.description: Independent small numerical examples of the identities, scope conditions and counterexamples; no random simulation or document rebuild.

simulation_archive.description: Validate and summarise the 20 archived diagnostic tables; does not run SLiM.

fresh_simulation.description: Run seeds 42–61 with SLiM 5.2, reconstruct diagnostics and compare every diagnostic table with the archive.

guide_figures.description: Regenerate all five mathematics-guide figures and check their stated values.

intro_checks.description: Print quadrature checks of one-trait population regressions and selected-parent weighting.

intro_figures.description: Rebuild three introductory teaching figures from their specified examples.

one_trait.description: Calculate and quadrature-check the three one-trait populations, then draw Figure A1.

geometry_values.description: Quadrature-check all rotation and comparison cases without rebuilding visual documents.

geometry_visuals.description: Rebuild the two-page geometry figure and offline explorer; Figure A2 is page one.

parental_weighting.description: Recover the fixed parental cloud, compare frequency and reproductive weights, and rebuild its figures and offline explorer.

estimation.description: Recreate the default observations, latent-value fit, 500 bootstrap refits and three estimation figures. The seed is 20261005; the bootstrap seed is 20261006.

estimation_checks.description: Run eight scientific checks: moments, observation/truth separation, independent integration, recovery, bootstrap calibration, quartic scope, integration failure and failed calibration.

quartic_case.description: Generate the optional misspecified quadratic analysis of data from a quartic log mean. These fitted results are an exploratory case; the cited 0.2424 is the exact generating full-curve R².

shiny.description: Launch the local Shiny for Python teaching app. Its download records the displayed data, settings, estimates and any completed bootstrap.

reference_comparison.description: After a complete default run, compare figure parameters/results, archived-simulation summary, observations and every bootstrap draw with the reference records.

results.title: Construct conditional expected fitness before taking logs
results.evidence_scope: Environmental-deviation samples illustrate phenotype-dependent assigned fitness. They are not offspring-count draws. The dashed curve is an analytic conditional mean.

results.title: Gaussian population projection identity
results.evidence_scope: 360 Gaussian scenarios (120 each in dimensions 2, 4 and 8), with 20,000 sampled individuals per scenario, compare the Gaussian expression with sample squared correlations. Finite sampling error is expected.

results.title: Proportional covariance contraction on a fixed surface
results.evidence_scope: The fitness surface and mean stay fixed; the narrow covariance is 0.11 times the broad covariance. This is proportional contraction, not an arbitrary reduction of total variance.

results.title: Scalar covariance trajectory with a separately changing gradient
results.evidence_scope: Four equal covariance directions follow the specified fixed-baseline scalar closure. The gradient is held constant through generation 40 and then changed separately; its decline is not generated by an offspring-mean recursion.

results.title: Conditional mean, logarithm and reproductive weighting
assumptions: Conditional expected output is positive where its logarithm is evaluated.
Selected-parent weighting requires a finite positive population mean output.
results.evidence_scope: Direct integration verifies a specified environmental average; discrete examples distinguish population frequencies from reproductive contributions. Log individual counts is a different target.

results.title: Gaussian environmental averaging changes breeding-value curvature
assumptions: Independent Gaussian environmental deviations.
Gaussian phenotype-dependent expected fitness.
results.evidence_scope: Finite numerical examples check the formula; the mathematical derivation is not replaced by computation.

results.title: Local quadratic approximation and the full nonquadratic curve
assumptions: The slope and Hessian are evaluated at the current population mean.
Population moments of the quadratic approximation need not equal those of the complete function.
results.evidence_scope: Finite numerical examples check the formula; the mathematical derivation is not replaced by computation.

results.title: Linear and centred-quadratic Gaussian moments
assumptions: Centred Gaussian breeding values and symmetric H.
The share has a positive total denominator.
results.evidence_scope: Finite numerical examples check the formula; the mathematical derivation is not replaced by computation.

results.title: Affine regression intercept, slope and R²
assumptions: Gaussian population weighting and a quadratic target.
An intercept is fitted; the tangent at the mean generally has a different intercept.
results.evidence_scope: Finite numerical examples check the formula; the mathematical derivation is not replaced by computation.

results.title: Noise reduces both R² values but their ratio recovers the share
assumptions: The response has the quadratic conditional mean plus a constant and zero conditional-mean residual.
Finite residual variance; for multiplicative noise, finite second moment of log U.
results.evidence_scope: An independent lognormal observation model verifies the constant-gap case. The identity does not justify taking logs of arbitrary individual offspring counts.

results.title: Proportional covariance scaling and the omitted fraction
assumptions: Mean, slope and Hessian stay fixed.
G is multiplied by one positive scalar.
Strict improvement under contraction requires both variance terms positive.
results.evidence_scope: Checks V_linear → s V_linear, V_quadratic → s² V_quadratic and share L/(L+sQ). The omitted fraction is sQ/(L+sQ), not a quantity that scales as s².

results.title: A smaller covariance can reduce the linear share
assumptions: b=(1,0), H=-I; compare I with diag(0.1,0.9).
results.evidence_scope: A numerical counterexample rules out extending proportional-scaling monotonicity to arbitrary covariance changes.

results.title: Changing trait units leaves the component variances unchanged
assumptions: An invertible linear change transforms G, b and H together.
results.evidence_scope: Finite numerical examples check the formula; the mathematical derivation is not replaced by computation.

results.title: Whitening, curvature eigenvalues and the separate Rayleigh quotient
assumptions: The whitened gradient norm and curvature spectrum are fixed in the no-alignment statement.
Rotating population covariance in fixed physical coordinates is a different comparison.
results.evidence_scope: The numerical examples distinguish coordinate invariance, physical rotation, and rotation at fixed whitened norms. The selected-parent error can change while the share is fixed.

results.title: Zero terms, undefined correlation and singular covariance support
locations: Main: boundaries of the variance share
assumptions: Inverse matrices and displacement norms are restricted to the varying support when G is singular.
results.evidence_scope: JSON null records an undefined quantity. A zero linear share is valid with positive quadratic variance, but the correlation expression then has a constant argument.

results.title: Asymmetry and non-Gaussian fourth moments can change the partition
results.evidence_scope: Two specified discrete distributions show why symmetry suffices for orthogonality but does not supply Gaussian fourth moments. They are counterexamples, not a general non-Gaussian estimator.

results.title: Exact selected-parent mean and covariance
assumptions: Gaussian initial breeding values.
An exactly log-quadratic conditional mean and positive-definite combined precision.
Covariance contraction additionally requires stabilising, positive-semidefinite curvature.
results.evidence_scope: Independent integration weights the original population. Both stabilising and integrable saddle examples are checked; a nonintegrable combined precision is identified.

results.title: A large share does not ensure an accurate parental shift or perfect rankings
results.evidence_scope: The exact quadratic Gaussian example gives a 50% relative parental displacement error. A separate pair in its tail reverses ranking; no claim is made about how frequent such reversals are.

results.title: Absolute covariance-weighted curvature bounds relative displacement error
assumptions: Exact Gaussian/log-quadratic closure with positive combined precision.
Nonzero full selected-parent displacement on the support of G.
Error and displacement use the same G-inverse norm.
results.evidence_scope: Checks relative error ≤ spectral norm of G^(1/2) Gamma G^(1/2) ≤ sqrt(2 V_quadratic), including equality along eigenvectors. The share alone is not this bound.

results.title: Fixed allelic effects do not imply fixed genic covariance
results.evidence_scope: The single-locus calculation isolates the frequency dependence of 2p(1-p)u². It does not claim to model frequency dynamics.

results.title: Fixed-baseline covariance interval and matrix fixed-point bounds
assumptions: Positive-definite fixed genic baseline B.
Fixed positive-semidefinite stabilising curvature.
Scalar retention 0 ≤ rho < 1 and the stated inheritance closure.
results.evidence_scope: Twelve cases check interval invariance for noncommuting matrices, and one numerical fixed point satisfies the bounds. General existence follows from the proof; general matrix uniqueness or convergence is not asserted.

results.title: Scalar fixed point, contraction and a transient increase
assumptions: B > 0, gamma ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ rho < 1.
The closed-form positive-root expression uses gamma > 0; gamma=0 gives B.
results.evidence_scope: Scalar contraction is checked directly for three pairs and from starts 0, 0.1 and 4. A low initial variance can increase; the model does not imply monotone contraction from every starting value.

results.title: No-restoration boundary and retained null-space variation
assumptions: rho=1 and constant positive-semidefinite curvature.
Positive initial covariance on its support.
results.evidence_scope: Repeated inversion is compared with G_t=(G_0^-1+t Gamma)^-1. Positive curvature removes all variation; a correlated singular-curvature example retains 1.84, not its initial marginal variance 2.

results.title: Prediction shrinkage can mimic proportional biological contraction
assumptions: Slope and curvature are known on the true breeding-value scale.
Only G is replaced by rG with 0<r<1.
results.evidence_scope: This substitution has a specified direction of error. It is not a universal correction when slopes/curvatures are refitted or reliabilities differ among directions.

results.title: Convert compatible phenotype regression moments to breeding-value parameters
assumptions: Joint Gaussian breeding values and phenotypes, with Cov(A,Z)=G.
Selection mediated by the measured phenotype or equivalent conditional-moment independence.
Same population, compatible unstandardised coordinates and the half-quadratic-form coefficient convention.
Selected covariance positive definite on the support.
Exact target derivatives additionally require the log-quadratic closure; otherwise these are moment-matched parameters.
results.evidence_scope: Positive-fitness examples in one and two traits independently integrate and fit the phenotype regression. The guide polynomial is a moment calculation and need not be positive in the tails; its raw log-polynomial derivatives differ from the converted parameters.

results.title: Two-stage estimation from repeated measurements and offspring counts
locations: SF3: Steps 1–4 and table of estimates
assumptions: The specified simulated trait is wholly additive; repeated independent measurement environments identify its variance in this teaching model.
Count likelihood integrates over latent breeding-value uncertainty; zero counts remain in the data.
The primary fitted family restricts H≤0.
results.evidence_scope: The generating breeding values are kept separate from the estimator. The calibrated latent-variable model, not observed plant height alone, supplies the breeding-value quantities. This is simulated data, not an empirical estimate.

results.title: Joint refitting and model-conditional uncertainty
locations: SF3: Step 5, intervals and component figure
results.evidence_scope: All 500 parametric replicates recalibrate measurement and genetic variance and refit the conditional mean. The interval reflects uncertainty under the fitted model, not uncertainty that the biological or quadratic model is correct.

results.title: Latent integration, recovery and explicit numerical failures
locations: SF3: likelihood calculation and integration checks
results.evidence_scope: Checks include a closed expected-output formula, an independent adaptive likelihood integral, the known-value limit, repeated-seed recovery, more quadrature points, and rejection of unresolved integration or failed variance calibration.
